page: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8559C processor operating at 3.2 GHz. This configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, with 2 threads per core. The processor includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions).

The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it bundles a 937 GB NVMe SSD, while network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results show a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core Geekbench score is in the top tier at 2299.0, and single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 decompression perform strongly. However, multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng is weak at 4390.87, and memory bandwidth for read-only large blocks is also weak at 33.73 GB/sec. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations both fall into the average category.

Given the high-speed DDR5 memory and local NVMe SSD storage, this instance offers a balanced profile for storage-heavy workloads, though multi-core scaling is limited by the 4 vCPU count. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high single-thread performance and fast local storage access rather than massive parallel compute. Appropriate workloads include database operations, text processing, static web serving, and small-to-medium language model prompt processing.
